hook: The soldier, slave and tax collector who wrote Don Quixote.

pages.x: Miguel de Cervantes was born in 1547 near Madrid, the son of a poor barber-surgeon. He became a soldier and, though sick with fever, fought at the sea battle of Lepanto in 1571. A shot crippled his left hand, and he was proud ever after to be "the one-handed man of Lepanto".
Sailing home in 1575, he was captured by pirates and taken to Algiers as a slave. He tried to escape four times, and each time took the blame himself, and was spared. In 1580 friars paid his ransom.

Back in Spain he wrote plays that flopped, then became a tax collector, buying grain for the Armada. Muddled accounts landed him in prison in Seville, where, he hinted, the idea for his great book was born.

In 1605 he published Don Quixote, about a poor gentleman who reads so many tales of knights that he decides to become one. With his plump squire, Sancho Panza, he rides out on a bony old horse to right the wrongs of the world. It was an instant hit.

In its most famous scene Don Quixote sees windmills and takes them for giants. He charges with his lance, and a turning sail flings him and his horse to the ground. To "tilt at windmills" still means to fight imaginary enemies.

In 1614 another writer published a fake second part. Furious, Cervantes rushed out his own Part Two, in which the real Don Quixote meets people who have read the fake one. He died in 1616, the same year as Shakespeare.
Don Quixote is often called the first modern novel and has been translated into more languages than almost any book but the Bible. Spanish is known as "the language of Cervantes".
pts: Wrote Don Quixote, often called the first modern novel
Fought at Lepanto and survived slavery in Algiers
The greatest writer in the Spanish language
